newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials hit high on bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials hit high on bullish sentiment.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares continued their bull run on Thursday, riding high on the back of falling money market rates drawing local institutional investors to the bourse and increasing interest from foreign investors as the local dollar stabilises, dealers said.
The key industrial index leapt 110.93 points -- a rise of 1.4 percent -- to a record high of 7,905.91.
"The market is very strong and we are now seeing a lot of foreigners coming back into the market as the Zimbabwe dollar stabilises," one broker said.
The local unit has over the past two weeks registered steady gains on key currencies after it fell heavily at the beginning of October.
Brokers said the beleagured rand of South Africa, Zimbabwe's major trading partner in Africa, had had no impact on trading on the local bourse.

Among Thursday's winners in industrials, bankers Barclays surged 200 cents to 2,400, publishing group Zimpapers leapt 100 cents to 2,100, clothing to furniture retailer Tedco rose 40 cents to 530 while timber producer Border and Alloys gained 25 cents each to 1,350 and 925 respectively.

Cement producer Porthold climbed 20 cents to 130, brick-maker Mash put on 15 cents to 175 while tea producer Tanganda at 300, soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes at 780, sugar firm Hippo at 890, battery-maker Chloride at 85 and rubber products company Acacia at 250 all added 10 cents.
Minings were quiet and largely unchanged, leaving the seven-counter mining index unmoved at 1,230.64.
